title: Coulomb's law; Electric potential and potential energy
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; F02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; F02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; F04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Volt
items.clue: Name of the unit equal to 1 J C⁻¹.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Single force found by adding each separate force as vectors.

items.label: Repulsion
items.clue: What happens between like charges, such as two positive ones.

items.label: Test charge
items.clue: Probe placed at P to sample V; its own size and sign do not affect the value.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres whose centres are 0.60 m apart exert electric forces of magnitude 1.0 N on each other. Their charges do not change. At what centre-to-centre separation would the forces have a magnitude of 9.0 N?

A point charge of +5.0 nC is fixed in place. A second charge of +2.0 nC is moved slowly from a point 0.30 m from the fixed charge to a point 0.10 m from it. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the work done on the +2.0 nC charge by the external force?

Three point charges are fixed on the x-axis: P (+4.0 nC) at x = 0, Q (+1.0 nC) at x = 0.10 m and R (+2.0 nC) at x = 0.30 m. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the magnitude of the resultant electric force on Q?

In a region of uniform electric field of strength 4.0 × 10³ V m⁻¹ directed in the +x direction, point A at x = 0 has an electric potential of +500 V. What is the electric potential at point B, at x = 0.050 m?

Two small charged spheres exert electric forces of magnitude F on each other. The charge on each sphere is halved, and the distance between them is reduced to one third of its value. What is the magnitude of the force now?
questions.explanation: Force ∝ (product of the charges)/r². Charges: ½ × ½ = ¼. Distance: 1/(⅓)² = 9. New force = 9F/4 ≈ 2.3F.
